newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC PREPARE FOR HAMBURG WITH 5-0 TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC PREPARE FOR HAMBURG WITH 5-0 TRIUMPH.

text.p: Celtic warmed up for their midweek UEFA Cup encounter with Bundesliga giants Hamburg by humiliating Hibernian 5-0 in the Scottish premier division on Saturday.
With Hamburg coach Felix Magath looking on from the stands at Parkhead, Celtic took the lead after four minutes through an own goal from one of their former players, Pat McGinlay.
It was the start of a disastrous afternoon for McGinlay, who was sent off nine minutes from time for his second bookable offence.

Celtic's Portuguese import Jorge Cadete added two first-half goals to take his tally for the season to nine, and the second period was a stroll in the bright September sunshine for Tommy Burns's team.
Brian O'Neil headed home Celtic's fourth goal five minutes after the break, and Dutchman Pierre Van Hooydonk claimed a fifth from a 72nd minute free-kick.
Victory took Celtic's unbeaten league run to 35 matches stretching back to September 30 last year when they lost to city-rivals Rangers.
The 5-0 win also shattered the achievement of Hibernian's Scotland international goalkeeper Jim Leighton, who had not conceded a goal in more than seven hours of play before Saturday.

The only dark cloud for Celtic was the departure on a stretcher of club record-signing Alan Stubbs, making his first start in a competitive game at Parkhead since arriving in Glasgow from Bolton Wanderers in the close season.
The injury could rule Stubbs out of Tuesday's UEFA Cup tie.
Champions Rangers recorded a modest 1-0 victory at Motherwell to preserve their 100 percent record.

Captain Richard Gough headed home the solitary goal in a largely uneventful game to keep Rangers two points clear of Celtic, and four ahead of Aberdeen, who enjoyed a 4-1 triumph at bottom club Raith Rovers.
